UNITED STATES PATENT OFFICE.
NIKOLA TESLA, OF NEW YORK, N. Y.
SYSTEM OF TRANSMISSION OF ELECTRICAL ENERGY.
SPECIFICATION forming part of Letters Patent No. 645,576, dated March 20, 1900.
Application filed September 2, 1897. Serial No. 650,343. (No model.)
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text:
To all whom it may concern:
Be it known that I, NIKOLA TESLA, a citizen of the United States, residing at New York, in the county and State of New York, have invented certain new and useful Improvements in Systems of Transmission of Electrical Energy, of which the following is a specification, reference being had to the drawing accompanying and forming a part of the same.
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: It has been well known heretofore that by rarefying the air inclosed in a vessel its insulating properties are impaired to such an extent that it becomes what may be considered as a true conductor, although one of admittedly very high resistance. The practical information in this regard has been derived from observations necessarily limited in their scope by the character of the apparatus or means heretofore known and the quality of the electrical effects producible thereby.
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: Thus it has been shown by William Crookes in his classical researches, which have so far served as the chief source of knowledge of this subject, that all gases behave as excellent insulators until rarefied to a point corresponding to about seventy-five millimeters, and even at this very low pressure the discharge of a high-tension induction-coil passes through only a part of the attenuated gas in the form of a luminous thread or arc, a still further and considerable diminution of the pressure being required to render the entire mass of the gas inclosed in a vessel conducting.
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: While this is true in every particular so long as electromotive or current impulses such as are obtainable with ordinary forms of apparatus are employed, I have found that neither the general behavior of the gases nor the known relations between electrical conductivity and barometric pressure are in conformity with these observations when impulses are used such as are producible by methods and apparatus devised by me and which have peculiar and hitherto unobserved properties and are of effective electromotive forces, measuring many hundred thousands or millions of volts. Through the actions of these current impulses I have been led to the discovery of certain highly important and useful facts which have hitherto been unknown.
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: Among these and bearing directly upon the subject of my present application are the following: First, that atmospheric or other gases, even under normal pressure, when they are known to behave as perfect insulators, are in a large measure deprived of their dielectric properties by being subjected to the influence of electromotive impulses of the character and magnitude I have
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: referred to and assume conducting and other qualities which have been so far observed only in gases greatly attenuated or heated to a high temperature, and, second, that the conductivity imparted to the air or other gases increases very rapidly both with the augmentation of the applied electrical pressure and with the degree of rarefaction, the law in this latter
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: In illustration of these facts a few observations, which I have made with apparatus devised for the purposes here contemplated, may be cited. For example, a conductor or terminal, to which impulses such as those here considered are supplied, but which is otherwise insulated in space and is remote from any conducting-bodies, is surrounded by a luminous flame-like brush or
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: discharge often covering many hundreds or even as much as several thousands of square feet of surface, this striking phenomenon clearly attesting the high degree of conductivity which the atmosphere attains under the influence of the immense electrical stresses to which it is subjected. This influence is, however, not confined to that portion of the atmosphere which is discernible by
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: the eye as luminous and which, as has been the case in some instances actually observed, may fill the space within a spherical or cylindrical envelop of a diameter of sixty feet or more, but reaches out to far remote regions, the insulating qualities of the air being, as I have ascertained, still sensibly impaired at a distance many hundred
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: times that through which the luminous discharge projects from the terminal and in all probability much farther.
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: Expressed briefly, my present invention, based upon these discoveries, consists then in producing at one point an electrical pressure of such character and magnitude as to cause thereby a current to traverse elevated strata of the air between the point of generation and a distant point at which the energy is to be received and utilized.
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: Referring to the drawing, A is a coil, generally of many turns and of a very large diameter, wound in spiral form about a magnetic core or not, as may be found necessary. C is a second coil, formed of a conductor of much larger section and smaller length, wound around and in proximity to the coil A. In the
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: transmitting apparatus the coil A constitutes the high-tension secondary and the coil C the primary of much lower tension of a transformer. In the circuit of the primary C is included a suitable source of current G. One terminal of the secondary A is at the center of the spiral coil, and from this terminal the current is led by
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: a conductor B to a terminal D, preferably of large surface, formed or maintained by such means as a balloon at an elevation suitable for the purposes of transmission, as before described. The other terminal of the secondary A is connected to earth and, if desired, also to the primary in order that the latter may be at substantially the
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: At the receiving-station a transformer of similar construction is employed; but in this case the coil A', of relatively-thin wire, constitutes the primary and the coil C', of thick wire or cable, the secondary of the transformer. In the circuit of the latter are included lamps L, motors M, or other devices for utilizing the current.
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: The elevated terminal D' is connected with the center of the coil A', and the other terminal of said coil is connected to earth and preferably, also, to the coil C' for the reasons above stated.
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: It will be observed that in coils of the character described the potential gradually increases with the number of turns toward the center, and the difference of potential between the adjacent turns being comparatively small a very high potential, impracticable with ordinary coils, may be successfully obtained. It will be, furthermore, noted that no matter to what an extent the
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: coils may be modified in design and construction, owing to their general arrangement and manner of connection, as illustrated, those portions of the wire or apparatus which are highly charged will be out of reach, while those parts of the same which are liable to be approached, touched, or handled will be at or nearly the same potential as the
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: adjacent portions of the ground, this insuring, both in the transmitting and receiving apparatus and regardless of the magnitude of the electrical pressure used, perfect personal safety, which is best evidenced by the fact that although such extreme pressures of many millions of volts have been for a number of years continuously experimented with no injury has been sustained neither
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: The length of the thin-wire coil in each transformer should be approximately one-quarter of the wave length of the electric disturbance in the circuit, this estimate being based on the velocity of propagation of the disturbance through the coil itself and the circuit with which it is designed to be used. By way of illustration, if the rate at which
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: the current traverses the circuit, including the coil, be one hundred and eighty-five thousand miles per second, then a frequency of nine hundred and twenty-five per second would maintain nine hundred and twenty-five stationary waves in a circuit one hundred and eighty-five thousand miles long and each wave would be two hundred miles in length. For such a low frequency,
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: to which I shall resort only when it is indispensable to operate motors of the ordinary kind under the conditions above assumed, I would use a secondary of fifty miles in length. By such an adjustment or proportioning of the length of wire in the secondary coil or coils the points of highest potential are made to coincide with the
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: elevated terminals D D', and it should be understood that whatever length be given to the wires this condition should be complied with in order to attain the best results.
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: As the main requirement in carrying out my invention is to produce currents of an excessively-high potential, this object will be facilitated by using a primary current of very considerable frequency, since the electromotive force obtainable with a given length of conductor is proportionate to the frequency; but the frequency of the current is in a large measure arbitrary, for if the potential be sufficiently high and if the terminals of the coils be maintained at the proper altitudes the action described will take place, and a current will be transmitted through the elevated air strata, which will encounter little and possibly even less resistance than if conveyed through a copper wire of a practicable size.
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: Accordingly the construction of the apparatus may be in many ways greatly varied; but in order to enable any person skilled in the mechanical and electrical arts to utilize to advantage in the practical applications of my system the experience I have so far gained in the carrying out of my invention on a large scale are given. The transmitting
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: apparatus was in this case one of my electrical oscillators, which are transformers of a special type, now well known and characterized by the passage of oscillatory discharges of a condenser through the primary. The source G, forming one of the elements of the transmitter, was a condenser of a capacity of about four one-hundredths of a microfarad and was
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: charged from a generator of alternating currents of fifty thousand volts pressure and discharged by means of a mechanically-operated break five thousand times per second through the primary C. The latter consisted of a single turn of stout stranded cable of inappreciable resistance and of an inductance of about eight thousand centimeters, the diameter of the loop being very nearly
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: two hundred and forty-four centimeters. The total inductance of the primary circuit was approximately ten thousand centimeters, so that the primary circuit vibrated generally, according to adjustment, from two hundred and thirty thousand to two hundred and fifty thousand times per second. The high-tension coil A in the form of a flat spiral was composed of fifty turns of heavily
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: insulated cable No. 8 wound in one single layer, the turns beginning close to the primary loop and ending near its center. The outer end of the secondary or high-tension coil A was connected to the ground, as illustrated, while the free end was led to a terminal placed in the rarefied air stratum through which the energy was to
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: be transmitted, which was contained in an insulating-tube of a length of fifty feet or more, within which a barometric pressure varying from about one hundred and twenty to one hundred and fifty millimeters was maintained by means of a mechanical suction-pump. The receiving-transformer was similarly proportioned, the ratio of conversion being the reciprocal of that of the transmitter, and
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: the primary high-tension coil A' was connected, as illustrated, with the end near the low-tension coil C' to the ground and with the free end to a wire or plate likewise placed in the rarefied air stratum and at the distance named from the transmitting-terminal. The primary and secondary circuits in the transmitting apparatus being carefully synchronized, an electromotive force
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: from two to four million volts and more was obtainable at the terminals of the secondary coil A, the discharge passing freely through the attenuated air stratum maintained at the above barometric pressures, and it was easy under these conditions to transmit with fair economy considerable amounts of energy, such as are of industrial moment, to the receiving apparatus for
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: supplying from the secondary coil C' lamps L or kindred devices. The results were particularly satisfactory when the primary coil or system A', with its secondary C', was carefully adjusted, so as to vibrate in synchronism with the transmitting coil or system A C. I have, however, found no difficulty in producing with apparatus of substantially the same design and
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: construction electromotive forces exceeding three or four times those before mentioned and have ascertained that by their means current impulses can be transmitted through much-denser air strata. By the use of these I have also found it practicable to transmit notable amounts of energy through air strata not in direct contact with the transmitting and receiving terminals, but remote from
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: them, the action of the impulses, in rendering conducting air of a density at which it normally behaves as an insulator, extending, as before remarked, to a considerable distance.
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: The high electromotive force obtained at the terminals of coil or conductor A was, as will be seen, in the preceding instance, not so much due to a large ratio of transformation as to the joint effect of the capacities and inductances in the synchronized circuits, which effect is enhanced by a high frequency, and it will be obviously understood
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: that if the latter be reduced a greater ratio of transformation should be resorted to, especially in cases in which it may be deemed of advantage to suppress as much as possible, and particularly in the transmitting-coil A, the rise of pressure due to the above effect and to obtain the necessary electromotive force solely by a large transformation ratio.
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: While electromotive forces such as are produced by the apparatus just described may be sufficient for many purposes to which my system will or may be applied, I wish to state that I contemplate using in an industrial undertaking of this kind greatly in excess of these, and with my present knowledge and experience in this novel field I would estimate them to range from twenty to fifty million volts and possibly more. By the use of these much greater forces larger amounts of energy may be conveyed through the atmosphere to remote places or regions, and the distance of transmission may be thus extended practically without limit.
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: As to the elevation of the terminals D D', it is obvious that it will be determined by a number of things, as by the amount and quality of the work to be performed, by the local density and other conditions of the atmosphere, by the character of the surrounding country, and such considerations as may present themselves in individual
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: instances. Thus if there be high mountains in the vicinity the terminals should be at a greater height, and generally they should always be, if practicable, at altitudes much greater than those of the highest objects near them in order to avoid as much as possible the loss by leakage. In some cases when small amounts of energy are required
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: the high elevation of the terminals, and more particularly of the receiving-terminal D', may not be necessary, since, especially when the frequency of the currents is very high, a sufficient amount of energy may be collected at that terminal by electrostatic induction from the upper air strata, which are rendered conducting by the active terminal of the transmitter or through
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: With reference to the facts which have been pointed out above it will be seen that the altitudes required for the transmission of considerable amounts of electrical energy in accordance with this method are such as are easily accessible and at which terminals can be safely maintained, as by the aid of captive balloons supplied continuously with gas from reservoirs
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: and held in position securely by steel wires or by any other means, devices, or expedients, such as may be contrived and perfected by ingenious and skilled engineers. From my experiments and observations I conclude that with electromotive impulses not greatly exceeding fifteen or twenty million volts the energy of many thousands of horse-power may be transmitted over vast distances,
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: measured by many hundreds and even thousands of miles, with terminals not more than thirty to thirty-five thousand feet above the level of the sea, and even this comparatively-small elevation will be required chiefly for reasons of economy, and, if desired, it may be considerably reduced, since by such means as have been described practically any potential that is desired
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: may be obtained, the currents through the air strata may be rendered very small, whereby the loss in the transmission may be reduced.
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: What I now claim is— 1. The method hereinbefore described of transmitting electrical energy through the natural media, which consists in producing at a generating-station a very high electrical pressure, causing thereby a propagation or flow of electrical energy, by conduction, through the earth and the air strata, and collecting or receiving at a distant point the electrical energy so propagated or caused to flow.
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: 2. The method hereinbefore described of transmitting electrical energy, which consists in producing at a generating-station a very high electrical pressure, conducting the current caused thereby to earth and to a terminal at an elevation at which the atmosphere serves as a conductor therefor, and collecting the current by a second elevated terminal at a distance from the first.
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text: 3. The method hereinbefore described of transmitting electrical energy through the natural media, which consists in producing between the earth and a generator-terminal elevated above the same, at a generating-station, a sufficiently-high electromotive force to render elevated air strata conducting, causing thereby a propagation or flow of electrical energy, by conduction, through the air strata, and collecting or receiving at a point distant from the generating-station the electrical energy so propagated or caused to flow.
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

attributes.text:
4. The method hereinbefore described of transmitting electrical energy through the natural media, which consists in producing between the earth and a generator-terminal elevated above the same, at a generating-station, a sufficiently-high electromotive force to render the air strata at or near the elevated terminal conducting, causing thereby a propagation or flow of electrical energy, by conduction, through the air strata, and collecting or receiving at a point distant from the generating-station the electrical energy so propagated or caused to flow. NIKOLA TESLA.
Witnesses:
M. LAWSON DYER,
G. W. MARTLING.
attributes.parent_title: System of Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1897/1900)

NIKOLA TESLA, OF NEW YORK, N. Y.
APPARATUS FOR TRANSMISSION OF ELECTRICAL ENERGY.
SPECIFICATION forming part of Letters Patent No. 649,621, dated May 15, 1900.
Original application filed September 2, 1897, Serial No. 650,343. Divided and this application filed February 19, 1900. Serial No. 5,780.
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1900)

attributes.text:
To all whom it may concern:
Be it known that I, NIKOLA TESLA, a citizen of the United States, residing at the borough of Manhattan, in the city, county and State of New York, have invented certain new and useful Improvements in Apparatus for the Transmission of Electrical Energy, of which the following is a specification, reference being had to the drawing accompanying and forming a part of the same.
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1900)

attributes.text: This application is a division of an application filed by me on September 2, 1897, Serial No. 650,343, entitled "Systems of transmission of electrical energy," and is based upon new and useful features and combinations of apparatus shown and described in said application for carrying out the method therein disclosed and claimed.
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1900)

attributes.text: The invention which forms the subject of my present application comprises a transmitting coil or conductor in which electrical currents or oscillations are produced and which is arranged to cause such currents or oscillations to be propagated by conduction through the natural medium from one point to another remote therefrom and a receiving coil or conductor adapted to be excited by the oscillations or currents propagated from the transmitter. This apparatus is shown in the accompanying drawing, which is a diagrammatic illustration of the same.
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1900)

attributes.text: A is a coil, generally of many turns and a very large diameter, wound in spiral form either about a magnetic core or not, as may be desired. C is a second coil formed by a conductor of much larger size and smaller length wound around and in proximity to the coil A. The apparatus at one point is used
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1900)

attributes.text: as a transmitter, the coil A in this case constituting a high-tension secondary, and the coil C the primary, of much lower tension, of a transformer. In the circuit of the primary C is included a suitable source of current G. One terminal of the secondary A is at the center of the spiral coil, and from this terminal the
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1900)

attributes.text: current is led by a conductor B to a terminal D, preferably of large surface, formed or maintained by such means as a balloon at an elevation suitable for the purposes of transmission. The other terminal of the secondary A is connected to earth and, if desired, to the primary also, in order that the latter may be at substantially
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1900)

attributes.text: the same potential as the adjacent portions of the secondary, thus insuring safety. At the receiving-station a transformer of similar construction is employed; but in this case the longer coil A' constitutes the primary, and the shorter coil C' the secondary, of the transformer. In the circuit of the latter are connected lamps L, motors M, or other devices for
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1900)

attributes.text: utilizing the current. The elevated terminal D' connects with the center of the coil A', and the other terminal of said coil is connected to earth and preferably, also, to the coil C' for the reasons above stated.

By way of illustration, if the rate at

attributes.text: which the current traverses the circuit including the coil be one hundred and eighty-five thousand miles per second then a frequency of nine hundred and twenty-five per second would maintain nine hundred and twenty-five stationary waves in a circuit one hundred and eighty-five thousand miles long and each wave would be two hundred miles in length. For such a low

attributes.text: frequency, which would be resorted to only when it is indispensable for the operation of motors of the ordinary kind under the conditions above assumed, I would use a secondary of fifty miles in length. By such an adjustment or proportioning of the length of wire in the secondary coil or coils the points of highest potential are made to
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1900)

attributes.text: coincide with the elevated terminals D D', and it should be understood that whatever length be given to the wires this requirement should be complied with in order to obtain the best results.
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1900)

attributes.text: It will be readily understood that when the above-prescribed relations exist the best conditions for resonance between the transmitting and receiving circuits are attained, and owing to the fact that the points of highest potential in the coils or conductors A A' are coincident with the elevated terminals the maximum flow of current will take place in the two coils, and this, further, necessarily implies that the capacity and inductance in each of the circuits have such values as to secure the most perfect condition of synchronism with the impressed oscillations.
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1900)

attributes.text: When the source of current G is in operation and produces rapidly pulsating or oscillating currents in the circuit of coil C, corresponding induced currents of very much higher potential are generated in the secondary coil A, and since the potential in the same gradually increases with the number of turns toward the center and the difference of potential between the adjacent turns is comparatively small a very high potential impracticable with ordinary coils may be successively obtained.
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1900)

attributes.text: As the main object for which the apparatus is designed is to produce a current of excessively high potential, this object is facilitated by using a primary current of very considerable frequency; but the frequency of the currents is in a large measure arbitrary, for if the potential be sufficiently high and the terminals of the coils be maintained at the proper elevation where the atmosphere is rarefied the stratum of air will serve as a conducting medium for the current produced and the latter will be transmitted through the air, with, it may be, even less resistance than through an ordinary conductor.
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1900)

attributes.text: As to the elevation of the terminals D D', it is obvious that this is a matter which will be determined by a number of things, as by the amount and quality of the work to be performed, by the condition of the atmosphere, and also by the character of the surrounding country. Thus if there be high mountains in
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1900)

attributes.text: the vicinity the terminals should be at a greater height, and generally they should always be, if practicable, at an altitude much greater than that of the highest objects near them. Since by the means described practically any potential that is desired may be produced, the currents through the air strata may be very small, thus reducing the loss in
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1900)

attributes.text: The apparatus at the receiving-station responds to the currents propagated from the transmitter in a manner which will be well understood from the foregoing description. The primary circuit of the receiver—that is, the thin wire coil A'—is excited by the currents propagated by conduction through the intervening natural medium from the transmitter, and these currents induce in the secondary coil C' other currents which are utilized for operating the devices included in the circuit thereof.
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1900)

attributes.text: Obviously the receiving-coils, transformers, or other apparatus may be movable—as, for instance, when they are carried by a vessel floating in the air or by a ship at sea. In the former case the connection of one terminal of the receiving apparatus to the ground might not be permanent, but may be intermittently or inductively established without departing from the spirit of my invention.
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1900)

attributes.text: It is to be noted that the phenomenon here involved in the transmission of electrical energy is one of true conduction and is not to be confounded with the phenomena of electrical radiation which have heretofore been observed and which from the very nature and mode of propagation would render practically impossible the transmission of any appreciable amount of energy to such distances as are of practical importance. What I now claim as my invention is—
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1900)

attributes.text: 1. The combination with a transmitting coil or conductor connected to ground and to an elevated terminal respectively, and means for producing therein electrical currents or oscillations, of a receiving coil or conductor similarly connected to ground and to an elevated terminal, at a distance from the transmitting-coil and adapted to be excited by currents caused to be propagated from the same by conduction through the intervening natural medium, a secondary conductor in inductive relation to the receiving-conductor and devices for utilizing the current in the circuit of said secondary conductor, as set forth.
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1900)

attributes.text: 2. The combination with a transmitting coil or conductor having its ends connected to ground and to an elevated terminal respectively, a primary coil in inductive relation thereto and a source of electrical oscillations in said primary circuit, of a receiving conductor or coil having its ends connected to ground and to an elevated terminal respectively and adapted to be excited by currents caused to be propagated from the transmitter through the natural medium and a secondary circuit in inductive relation to the receiving-circuit and receiving devices connected therewith, as set forth.
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1900)

attributes.text: 3. The combination with a transmitting instrument comprising a transformer having its secondary connected to ground and to an elevated terminal respectively, and means for impressing electrical oscillations upon its primary, of a receiving instrument comprising a transformer having its primary similarly connected to ground and to an elevated terminal, and a translating device connected with its secondary, the capacity and inductance of the two transformers having such values as to secure synchronism with the impressed oscillations, as set forth.
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1900)

attributes.text: 4. The combination with a transmitting instrument comprising an electrical transformer having its secondary connected to ground and to an elevated terminal respectively, and means for impressing electrical oscillations upon its primary, of a receiving instrument comprising a transformer having its primary similarly connected to ground and to an elevated terminal, and a translating device connected with its secondary, the capacity and inductance of the secondary of the transmitting and primary of the receiving instruments having such values as to secure synchronism with the impressed oscillations, as set forth.
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1900)

attributes.text: 5. The combination with a transmitting coil or conductor connected to ground and to an elevated terminal respectively, and means for producing electrical currents or oscillations in the same, of a receiving coil or conductor similarly connected to ground and to an elevated terminal and synchronized with the transmitting coil or conductor, as set forth.
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1900)

attributes.text: 6. The combination with a transmitting instrument comprising an electrical transformer having its secondary connected to ground and to an elevated terminal respectively, of a receiving instrument comprising a transformer, having its primary similarly connected to ground and to an elevated terminal, the receiving-coil being synchronized with that of the transmitter, as set forth.
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmission of Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1900)

attributes.text: 7. The combination with a transmitting coil or conductor connected to ground and to an elevated terminal respectively, and means for producing electrical currents or oscillations in the same, of a receiving coil or conductor similarly connected to ground and to an elevated terminal, the said coil or coils having a length equal to one-quarter of the wave length of the disturbance propagated, as set forth.

To all whom it may concern:
Be it known that I, NIKOLA TESLA, a citizen of the United States, residing in the borough of Manhattan, in the city, county, and State of New York, have invented certain new and useful Improvements in Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy, of which the following is a specification, reference being had to the drawing accompanying and forming a part of the same.
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

attributes.text: In endeavoring to adapt currents or discharges of very high tension to various valuable uses, as the distribution of energy through wires from central plants to distant places of consumption, or the transmission of powerful disturbances to great distances, through the natural or non-artificial media, I have encountered difficulties in confining considerable amounts of electricity to the conductors and preventing its leakage over their supports, or its escape into the ambient air, which always takes place when the electric surface density reaches a certain value.
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

attributes.text: The intensity of the effect of a transmitting circuit with a free or elevated terminal is proportionate to the quantity of electricity displaced, which is determined by the product of the capacity of the circuit, the pressure, and the frequency of the currents employed. To produce an electrical movement of the required magnitude it is desirable to charge the terminal
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

attributes.text: as highly as possible, for while a great quantity of electricity may also be displaced by a large capacity charged to low pressure, there are disadvantages met with in many cases when the former is made too large. The chief of these are due to the fact that an increase of the capacity entails a lowering of the frequency of
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

attributes.text: the impulses or discharges and a diminution of the energy of vibration. This will be understood when it is borne in mind, that a circuit with a large capacity behaves as a slack spring, whereas one with a small capacity acts like a stiff spring, vibrating more vigorously. Therefore, in order to attain the highest possible frequency, which for certain
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

attributes.text: purposes is advantageous and, apart from that, to develop the greatest energy in such a transmitting circuit, I employ a terminal of relatively small capacity, which I charge to as high a pressure as practicable. To accomplish this result I have found it imperative to so construct the elevated conductor, that its outer surface, on which the electrical charge chiefly
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

attributes.text: accumulates, has itself a large radius of curvature, or is composed of separate elements which, irrespective of their own radius of curvature, are arranged in close proximity to each other and so, that the outside ideal surface enveloping them is of a large radius. Evidently, the smaller the radius of curvature the greater, for a given electric displacement, will be
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

attributes.text: the surface-density and, consequently, the lower, the limiting pressure to which the terminal may be charged without electricity escaping into the air. Such a terminal I secure to an insulating support entering more or less into its interior, and I likewise connect the circuit to it inside or, generally, at points where the electric density is small. This plan of
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

attributes.text: constructing and supporting a highly charged conductor I have found to be of great practical importance, and it may be usefully applied in many ways.
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

attributes.text: Referring to the accompanying drawing, the figure is a view in elevation and part section of an improved free terminal and circuit of large surface with supporting structure and generating apparatus.
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

attributes.text: The terminal D consists of a suitably shaped metallic frame, in this case a ring of nearly circular cross section, which is covered with half spherical metal plates P P, thus constituting a very large conducting surface, smooth on all places where the electric charge principally accumulates. The frame is carried by a strong platform expressly provided for safety appliances, instruments of observation, etc., which in turn rests on insulating supports F F. These should penetrate far into the hollow space formed by the terminal, and if the electric density at the points where they are bolted to the frame is still considerable, they may be specially protected by conducting hoods as H.
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

attributes.text: Apart of the improvements which form the subject of this specification, the transmitting circuit, in its general features, is identical with that described and claimed in my original Patents Nos. 645,576 and 649,621. The circuit comprises a coil A which is in close inductive relation with a primary C, and one end of which is connected to a ground-plate E,
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

attributes.text: while its other end is led through a separate self-induction coil B and a metallic cylinder B' to the terminal D. The connection to the latter should always be made at, or near the center, in order to secure a symmetrical distribution of the current, as otherwise, when the frequency is very high and the flow of large volume, the
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

attributes.text: performance of the apparatus might be impaired. The primary C may be excited in any desired manner, from a suitable source of currents G, which may be an alternator or condenser, the important requirement being that the resonant condition is established, that is to say, that the terminal D is charged to the maximum pressure developed in the circuit, as
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

attributes.text: I have specified in my original patents before referred to. The adjustments should be made with particular care when the transmitter is one of great power, not only on account of economy, but also in order to avoid danger. I have shown that it is practicable to produce in a resonating circuit as E A B B' D immense electrical
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

attributes.text: activities, measured by tens and even hundreds of thousands of horse-power, and in such a case, if the points of maximum pressure should be shifted below the terminal D, along coil B, a ball of fire might break out and destroy the support F or anything else in the way. For the better appreciation of the nature of this danger
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

attributes.text: it should be stated, that the destructive action may take place with inconceivable violence. This will cease to be surprising when it is borne in mind, that the entire energy accumulated in the excited circuit, instead of requiring, as under normal working conditions, one quarter of the period or more for its transformation from static to kinetic form, may spend
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

attributes.text: itself in an incomparably smaller interval of time, at a rate of many millions of horse power. The accident is apt to occur when, the transmitting circuit being strongly excited, the impressed oscillations upon it are caused, in any manner more or less sudden, to be more rapid than the free oscillations. It is therefore advisable to begin the adjustments
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

attributes.text: with feeble and somewhat slower impressed oscillations, strengthening and quickening them gradually, until the apparatus has been brought under perfect control. To increase the safety, I provide on a convenient place, preferably on terminal D, one or more elements or plates either of somewhat smaller radius of curvature or protruding more or less beyond the others (in which case they
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

attributes.text: may be of larger radius of curvature) so that, should the pressure rise to a value, beyond which it is not desired to go, the powerful discharge may dart out there and lose itself harmlessly in the air. Such a plate, performing a function similar to that of a safety valve on a high pressure reservoir, is indicated at V.
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

attributes.text: Still further extending the principles underlying my invention, special reference is made to coil B and conductor B'. The latter is in the form of a cylinder with smooth or polished surface of a radius much larger than that of the half spherical elements P P, and widens out at the bottom into a hood H, which should be slotted
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

attributes.text: to avoid loss by eddy currents and the purpose of which will be clear from the foregoing. The coil B is wound on a frame or drum D1 of insulating material, with its turns close together. I have discovered that when so wound the effect of the small radius of curvature of the wire itself is overcome and the coil
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

attributes.text: behaves as a conductor of large radius of curvature, corresponding to that of the drum. This feature is of considerable practical importance and is applicable not only in this special instance, but generally. For example, such plates as P P of terminal D, though preferably of large radius of curvature, need not be necessarily so, for provided only that the
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

attributes.text: individual plates or elements of a high potential conductor or terminal are arranged in proximity to each other and with their outer boundaries along an ideal symmetrical enveloping surface of a large radius of curvature, the advantages of the invention will be more or less fully realized. The lower end of the coil B—which, if desired, may be extended up
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

attributes.text: to the terminal D—should be somewhat below the uppermost turn of coil A. This, I find, lessens the tendency of the charge to break out from the wire connecting both and to pass along the support F.
attributes.parent_title: Apparatus for Transmitting Electrical Energy (Tesla, 1902/1914) - Wardenclyffe

As a means for producing great electrical activities a resonant circuit having its outer conducting boundaries, which are charged to a high potential, arranged in surfaces of large radii of curvature so as to prevent leakage of the oscillating charge, substantially as set forth.

UNITED STATES PATENT
US 9,923,385 B2
EXCITATION AND USE OF GUIDED SURFACE WAVES
Inventors: James F. Corum, Kenneth L. Corum
Assignee: CPG Technologies, LLC
Filed: June 2, 2015
Issued: March 20, 2018 ABSTRACT
Disclosed are various embodiments for transmitting and receiving energy conveyed in the form of a guided surface-waveguide mode along the surface of a lossy medium such as, e.g., a terrestrial medium excited by a guided surface waveguide probe.
attributes.parent_title: Excitation and Use of Guided Surface Waves (Corum, 2015/2018)

attributes.text:
BACKGROUND
For over a century, signals transmitted by radio waves involved radiation fields launched using conventional antenna structures. In contrast to radio science, electrical power distribution systems in the last century involved the transmission of energy guided along electrical conductors. This understanding of the distinction between radio frequency (RF) and power transmission has existed since the early 1900's. KEY DISTINCTION: GUIDED vs RADIATED WAVES
attributes.parent_title: Excitation and Use of Guided Surface Waves (Corum, 2015/2018)

attributes.text: Guided electromagnetic fields: a propagating electromagnetic wave whose energy is concentrated within or near boundaries between media having different electromagnetic properties. In this sense, a guided electromagnetic field is one that is bound to a waveguide and may be characterized as being conveyed by the current flowing in the waveguide. If there is no load for a guided electromagnetic wave, then no energy is consumed.
attributes.parent_title: Excitation and Use of Guided Surface Waves (Corum, 2015/2018)

attributes.text: Radiated electromagnetic fields: electromagnetic energy that is emitted from a source structure in the form of waves that are not bound to a waveguide. Radiated electromagnetic fields are characterized by free electromagnetic fields that emanate from the source structure and spread out in space. Once radiated, these waves propagate independently of the receiver and are lost regardless of whether a receiver is present. The surface wave in the Zenneck-Sommerfeld guided wave sense is distinct from ground wave propagation in the Weyl-Norton-FCC sense.
attributes.parent_title: Excitation and Use of Guided Surface Waves (Corum, 2015/2018)

attributes.text:
FREQUENCY SPECIFICATIONS
Example operating frequency: 1.85 MHz. At 1.85 MHz the free-space wavelength is approximately 162 meters. The guided surface wave probe is designed to match the complex Brewster angle at this frequency.
attributes.parent_title: Excitation and Use of Guided Surface Waves (Corum, 2015/2018)

attributes.text:
TERMINAL GEOMETRY
Charge terminal T1 specifications:
- Shape: sphere, disk, cylinder, cone, torus, hood, one or more rings, or any other randomized shape
- Height requirement: at least four times the spherical diameter
- Self-capacitance varies with elevation above ground plane
- Coupling to earth via feed network with polyphase excitation synthesizing fields at the complex Brewster angle
attributes.parent_title: Excitation and Use of Guided Surface Waves (Corum, 2015/2018)

attributes.text: The guided surface waveguide probe includes a charge terminal T1 elevated above a lossy conducting medium. The charge terminal T1 is coupled to an excitation source via a feed network. The feed network comprises a receiver network coupled between the charge terminal T1 and the lossy conducting medium with the charge terminal T1 being positioned such that charge is distributed across the charge terminal T1.
attributes.parent_title: Excitation and Use of Guided Surface Waves (Corum, 2015/2018)

attributes.text:
HISTORICAL REFERENCES
Zenneck, Jonathan (1907): "Uber die Fortpflanzung ebener elektromagnetischer Wellen längs einer ebenen Leiterfläche und ihre Beziehung zur drahtlosen Telegraphie"
Sommerfeld, A. (1909): "Uber die Ausbreitung der Wellen in der Drahtlosen Telegraphie"

Cullen, A.L. (1954): "The Excitation of Plane Surface Waves"

CLAIMS (summary)
1. A method of transmitting energy comprising launching a guided surface wave along a surface of a lossy conducting medium using a guided surface waveguide probe having a charge terminal elevated above the lossy conducting medium and configured to generate a wavefront incident on the surface at the complex Brewster angle of the lossy conducting medium.
attributes.parent_title: Excitation and Use of Guided Surface Waves (Corum, 2015/2018)

attributes.text: 2. A guided surface waveguide probe comprising a charge terminal elevated above a lossy conducting medium and a feed network coupled to the charge terminal configured to generate a wavefront incident at the complex Brewster angle at a frequency of operation. 3. The probe of claim 2 wherein the frequency of operation is in the range of 0.1 MHz to 10 MHz. 4. The probe of claim 2 wherein the charge terminal comprises a sphere having a diameter.
attributes.parent_title: Excitation and Use of Guided Surface Waves (Corum, 2015/2018)

attributes.text: 5. The probe of claim 2 wherein the feed network comprises a coil having inductance. 6. The probe of claim 2 wherein the wavefront substantially mode-matches a Zenneck surface wave bound to the interface between the lossy conducting medium and an insulating medium above the lossy conducting medium. 7. A method of receiving energy guided along a lossy conducting medium as a guided surface wave, comprising extracting electrical energy from the guided surface wave using a guided surface waveguide receiver.
attributes.parent_title: Excitation and Use of Guided Surface Waves (Corum, 2015/2018)

attributes.text: The disclosed apparatus launches a Zenneck surface wave that propagates as a bound mode along the lossy medium (earth) interface with the insulating medium (atmosphere). The non-radiative nature of the bound mode enables efficient energy transmission to distant receivers with minimal losses that scale as 1/sqrt(distance) rather than 1/distance squared as in ordinary radio transmission. This method is distinguished from radiated wave transmission by the fact that the guided surface wave is bound to the waveguide interface and does not lose energy through radiation into free space.
attributes.parent_title: Excitation and Use of Guided Surface Waves (Corum, 2015/2018)

ABSTRACT
Disclosed are various embodiments for launching a guided surface wave along a surface of a lossy conducting medium. The apparatus includes a guided surface waveguide probe configured to excite a guided surface wave having at least one field component that is bound to the interface between the lossy conducting medium and an insulating medium. BACKGROUND
attributes.parent_title: Excitation and Use of Guided Surface Wave Modes on Lossy Media (Corum, 2013/2018)

attributes.text: For over a century, signals transmitted by radio waves involved radiation fields launched using conventional antenna structures. The use of radiated electromagnetic waves for the transmission of energy has been deemed impractical due to the inverse square law of radiation loss: energy transmitted via radiated waves spreads out in three dimensions and dissipates rapidly with distance.
attributes.parent_title: Excitation and Use of Guided Surface Wave Modes on Lossy Media (Corum, 2013/2018)

attributes.text: In contrast to ordinary radio transmission, the present invention concerns the launching of guided surface waves along the interface between two media of different electromagnetic properties. A guided surface wave is a bound propagating mode whose energy is concentrated near the interface and which decays exponentially with distance above the surface. DEFINITIONS AND DISTINCTIONS
attributes.parent_title: Excitation and Use of Guided Surface Wave Modes on Lossy Media (Corum, 2013/2018)

attributes.text: A guided electromagnetic field is a propagating electromagnetic wave whose energy is concentrated within or near boundaries between media having different electromagnetic properties. In this sense, a guided electromagnetic field is one that is bound to a waveguide. If there is no load for a guided electromagnetic wave, then no energy is consumed at the waveguide.
attributes.parent_title: Excitation and Use of Guided Surface Wave Modes on Lossy Media (Corum, 2013/2018)

attributes.text: A radiated electromagnetic field comprises electromagnetic energy that is emitted from a source structure in the form of waves that are not bound to a waveguide. Radiated electromagnetic fields characteristically free propagate through space independent of the source. Once radiated, these fields propagate outward and are lost regardless of whether a receiver is present.
attributes.parent_title: Excitation and Use of Guided Surface Wave Modes on Lossy Media (Corum, 2013/2018)

attributes.text: Field strength characteristics distinguish the two modes decisively. For a guided surface wave, the field strength as a function of distance d from the launching apparatus falls off at a rate of approximately exp(−αd) / sqrt(d), where α is an attenuation constant dependent on the conductivity of the lossy medium. For a radiated wave, the field strength falls off at a rate of 1/d (for the far field), which corresponds to a 1/d² reduction in power.
attributes.parent_title: Excitation and Use of Guided Surface Wave Modes on Lossy Media (Corum, 2013/2018)

attributes.text: The guided surface wave considered here is of the Zenneck-Sommerfeld type, distinguished from the conventional Norton ground wave and from ordinary radio wave propagation. GUIDED SURFACE WAVEGUIDE PROBE
attributes.parent_title: Excitation and Use of Guided Surface Wave Modes on Lossy Media (Corum, 2013/2018)

attributes.text: A guided surface waveguide probe comprises a charge terminal T1 elevated above a lossy conducting medium, coupled to an excitation source via a feed network. The charge terminal T1 is positioned at a height relative to the lossy conducting medium such that electromagnetic waves emitted from the probe are launched at the complex Brewster angle of incidence at the interface between the lossy conducting medium and an insulating medium above the lossy conducting medium.
attributes.parent_title: Excitation and Use of Guided Surface Wave Modes on Lossy Media (Corum, 2013/2018)

attributes.text:
When the complex Brewster angle condition is satisfied, the wavefront emitted from the charge terminal substantially mode-matches a Zenneck surface wave bound to the interface. This mode-matching condition is the critical design requirement of the invention. FREQUENCY SPECIFICATIONS Example operating frequencies include 1.85 MHz and 59 MHz. At these frequencies:
- 1.85 MHz: free-space wavelength ≈ 162 meters
- 59 MHz: free-space wavelength ≈ 5.08 meters
attributes.parent_title: Excitation and Use of Guided Surface Wave Modes on Lossy Media (Corum, 2013/2018)

attributes.text: The frequency of operation is selected such that the charge terminal height and the feed network parameters establish the complex Brewster angle condition at the desired operating frequency. TERMINAL GEOMETRY The charge terminal T1 may comprise a sphere, a disk, a cylinder, a cone, a torus, a hood, one or more rings, or any other randomized shape. The charge terminal is characterized by its self-capacitance C1, which depends on its shape, size, and height above ground.

attributes.text: The charge terminal is placed at a height above the lossy conducting medium such that bound surface charge is coupled to the surface of the lossy conducting medium via the feed network. The height of the charge terminal is selected to establish the complex Brewster angle at the operating frequency. FEED NETWORK
attributes.parent_title: Excitation and Use of Guided Surface Wave Modes on Lossy Media (Corum, 2013/2018)

attributes.text: The feed network comprises an inductor coupled between an excitation source and the charge terminal T1. The feed network is configured to generate a phase delay such that the wavefront incident on the lossy conducting medium satisfies the complex Brewster angle condition. In various embodiments, the feed network comprises a helical coil configured as a slow-wave structure. The helical coil has a phase velocity less than the speed of light in free space, allowing a compact physical implementation of a distributed transmission line with a specified electrical length. Inventors: James F. Corum, Kenneth L. Corum

Issued: September 25, 2018 ABSTRACT
Disclosed are guided surface waveguide probes configured to excite electromagnetic fields that couple into guided surface waveguide modes along lossy conducting media such as Earth. These probes synthesize electric fields at complex Brewster angles of incidence, enabling energy transmission as bound surface waves rather than radiated fields. KEY TECHNICAL DISTINCTIONS

attributes.text: Guided vs Radiated Fields: A guided electromagnetic field is one that is bound to a waveguide with energy concentrated near boundaries between media with different electromagnetic properties. In contrast, radiated fields spread geometrically (1/d decay) while guided fields exhibit exponential decay of e^(-d/sqrt(d)), producing a distinctive "knee" on field strength curves that is the signature of bound surface wave propagation.

attributes.text: Core Physical Basis: The work references foundational theory from Jonathan Zenneck (1907) regarding electromagnetic wave propagation along flat conducting surfaces, and Sommerfeld's analysis of wireless telegraphy propagation phenomena. attributes.text:
Charge Terminal Configuration:
- Elevated charge terminal T1 positioned along vertical axis normal to ground plane
- Physical height at least four to five times the effective spherical diameter to reduce bound charge
- Self-capacitance relationship: C = 4*pi*epsilon0*a where a is terminal radius

attributes.text:
Wave Tilt Angle (tau):
The wave tilt at Hankel crossover distance relates to complex effective height through:
- tau = phase angle of complex effective height (h_eff)
- h_eff = (1/I0*lambda0) * integral of I(z)*exp(j*beta*z) dz over physical height
- Velocity factor Vf typically approximately 0.93-0.98 for wire conductors

attributes.text:
Brewster Angle Matching:
At complex Brewster angle theta_i,B, reflection coefficient approaches zero. The incident electric field must satisfy:
- Wave front incident at Hankel crossover distance Rx
- Phase matching between field polarization and medium impedance
- Zero or negligible reflection enabling efficient mode coupling into the bound surface wave mode FREQUENCY-DEPENDENT PARAMETERS
attributes.parent_title: Modulated Guided Surface Waves (Corum, 2018)

attributes.text:
Example calculations at 1.85 MHz:
- Wavelength lambda0 drives geometric scaling
- Hankel crossover distance Rx varies with conductivity (sigma) and permittivity (epsilon_r) of lossy medium
- Phase constants: beta_w = 2*pi*f/c*Vw (wire), beta_c for coil structures
- Operating frequency must align phase delay curves for tau = phi crossing FEED NETWORK COMPONENTS Helical Coil (Phase Delay Circuit):
- Velocity factor: Vf = (H/D) / (N*lambda0) where H=axial length, D=diameter, N=turns
- Phase delay: phi_c relates to spatial configuration
- Characteristic impedance: Zc varies with frequency

attributes.text:
Vertical Feed Line Conductor:
- Single-wire impedance: Zw = (120/pi) * ln(2h/a) for height h, radius a
- Phase constant: beta_w = 2*pi*f*Vw/c*lambda0 MODE-MATCHING CONDITION The probe achieves efficient coupling when:
1. Electrical effective height generates the required wave tilt angle
2. Phase delay (phi_U for coil, phi_y for wire) matches wave tilt angle tau
3. Impedance resonance with respect to complex image ground plane at depth z1 below surface
4. Image plane approximation: z1 approximately lambda0 / (2*pi*sqrt(sigma1/(omega*epsilon0))) RECEIVER STRUCTURES

Disclosed are methods to launch electromagnetic energy as guided surface waves, also termed Zenneck surface wave modes, along conductive media like Earth, rather than radiating energy into free space. attributes.text: The patent describes methods to launch electromagnetic energy as guided surface waves along conductive media like Earth, rather than radiating energy into free space. attributes.text: Guided electromagnetic fields remain concentrated within or near boundaries between media having different electromagnetic properties. Radiated fields spread geometrically and dissipate regardless of receiver presence. Guided surface waves fall off exponentially as exp(-alpha*d)/sqrt(d), while radiated fields decrease at 1/d for field strength (1/d^2 for power).

attributes.text: The distinction between guided and radiated electromagnetic waves is physical and fundamental. A guided wave is a bound mode of propagation along a waveguide structure (in this case the Earth-air interface). A radiated wave is a free-space wave that propagates independently of its source and is lost if not intercepted. This fundamental physical distinction is the basis of the present invention. attributes.text:
UNITED STATES PATENT
US 7,741,734 B2
WIRELESS NON-RADIATIVE ENERGY TRANSFER
Inventors: Marin Soljacic, Aristeidis Karalis, John D. Joannopoulos
Assignee: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (later licensed to WiTricity Corp)
Issued: June 22, 2010 ABSTRACT
The patent describes electromagnetic energy transfer between two resonator structures separated by distances larger than their characteristic sizes. Energy transfers through coupling of resonant-field evanescent tails rather than radiative means, enabling mid-range wireless power delivery using high-Q electromagnetic resonators. BACKGROUND
attributes.parent_title: Wireless Non-Radiative Energy Transfer (Soljacic/MIT, 2010)

attributes.text: Previous wireless power approaches have significant limitations: radiative antenna schemes waste energy into free space due to the inverse square law; directed radiation such as lasers or microwave beams requires line-of-sight and precise pointing; traditional induction operates only at very close range where the transmission distance is much less than the device dimensions (L_TRANS much less than L_DEV).
attributes.parent_title: Wireless Non-Radiative Energy Transfer (Soljacic/MIT, 2010)

attributes.text: The present invention addresses these limitations by using resonant coupling between high-Q electromagnetic structures. Energy is transferred through the coupling of the evanescent near-field tails of two resonant structures tuned to the same frequency. This approach enables mid-range operation where the transmission distance is a few times the device characteristic size. KEY TECHNICAL MECHANISM Coupling Approach: The system uses resonant coupling between high-Q structures. As stated: "two same-frequency resonant objects tend to couple, while interacting weakly with off-resonant environmental objects."
attributes.parent_title: Wireless Non-Radiative Energy Transfer (Soljacic/MIT, 2010)

attributes.text: Distance Capability: The transfer distance D must satisfy D less than lambda1 and D less than lambda2 where lambda represents resonant wavelength. This enables coupling at distances larger than the characteristic size of each resonator but within the near-field region where evanescent fields dominate.
attributes.parent_title: Wireless Non-Radiative Energy Transfer (Soljacic/MIT, 2010)

attributes.text:
Non-Radiative Nature: This is a non-radiative wireless power transfer mechanism. The energy transfer occurs through the evanescent fields of the resonators, not through radiating waves. Both resonators must be within each other's "radiation caustic" boundary where fields decay exponentially before becoming oscillatory. No propagating electromagnetic wave is emitted into free space. RESONATOR IMPLEMENTATIONS Dielectric Disk Cavities:
- Support whispering-gallery modes with high radiation-Q values
- Demonstrated: Q=1992, lambda/r=20
- Permittivity values: epsilon approximately 65-147
- Operating principle: TE-polarized modes with slow azimuthal field variations
attributes.parent_title: Wireless Non-Radiative Energy Transfer (Soljacic/MIT, 2010)

attributes.text:
Capacitively-Loaded Conducting Wire Loops:
- Single-coil copper designs with quality factors Q approximately 1000-1500
- Operating frequencies: 5 MHz for 1 m loops, 17 MHz for 30 cm loops, 380 MHz for 1 cm loops
- Characteristic wavelength ratios: lambda/r approximately 50-80 for near-field coupling COUPLING PARAMETERS The coupling coefficient kappa represents the energy transfer rate between the two resonators. The critical performance metric kappa/sqrt(Gamma1*Gamma2) must exceed 0.2-5 depending on application requirements. For dielectric disks at separation D/r=10: kappa/Gamma approximately 1.16
For dielectric disks at separation D/r=3: kappa/Gamma approximately 42.49
attributes.parent_title: Wireless Non-Radiative Energy Transfer (Soljacic/MIT, 2010)

attributes.text:
LOSS MECHANISMS - Radiation losses: From mode leakage into free space
- Ohmic losses: Resistive heating in conductors
- Material absorption: Bulk dielectric losses Achievable efficiency: at least 40% for optimized dielectric disk systems with medium-range distances (D/r less than 10). CRITICAL DISTINCTION FROM SURFACE-WAVE SYSTEMS This technology uses evanescent field coupling of electromagnetic resonances. This is NOT surface wave propagation. The energy does not travel along a conducting interface. The energy couples between two discrete resonators through their near-field tails.
attributes.parent_title: Wireless Non-Radiative Energy Transfer (Soljacic/MIT, 2010)

attributes.text: The key difference: surface waves propagate along an interface (e.g., Earth-air) and can travel long distances; evanescent coupling occurs between two specific resonators that must both be within each other's near-field region. The surface wave is a propagating mode along a waveguide; the evanescent coupling is a localized exchange between paired oscillators. SAFETY ADVANTAGE Human safety advantage of magnetic loop systems: "Humans are also non-magnetic and can sustain strong magnetic fields without undergoing any risk." This makes magnetic near-field coupling preferable to electric field coupling for applications near biological tissue.
attributes.parent_title: Wireless Non-Radiative Energy Transfer (Soljacic/MIT, 2010)

UNITED STATES PATENT
US 8,686,598 B2
WIRELESS ENERGY TRANSFER FOR SUPPLYING POWER AND HEAT TO A DEVICE
Assignee: WiTricity Corp
Issued: April 1, 2014 ABSTRACT
Described is a non-radiative, or near-field, wireless energy transfer scheme using coupled electromagnetic resonators. The system transfers power through oscillating magnetic fields rather than radiative transmission, making it fundamentally different from broadcast wireless power systems. CORE TECHNOLOGY
attributes.parent_title: Wireless Energy Transfer for Supplying Power and Heat (WiTricity, 2014)

attributes.text: The technology employs coupled electromagnetic resonators with long-lived oscillatory resonant modes to mediate energy transfer. The resonators are specifically designed such that the energy stored by the electric field is primarily confined within the structure and that the energy stored by the magnetic field is primarily in the region surrounding the resonator, enabling energy exchange mediated primarily by the resonant magnetic near-field.
attributes.parent_title: Wireless Energy Transfer for Supplying Power and Heat (WiTricity, 2014)

attributes.text: This is a non-radiative wireless power transfer system. Energy is not radiated into free space. Instead, energy is transferred through the overlapping magnetic near-fields of two tuned resonators. The system cannot transmit to distances larger than the near-field region (typically a wavelength). TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS
attributes.parent_title: Wireless Energy Transfer for Supplying Power and Heat (WiTricity, 2014)

attributes.text:
Resonator Characteristics:
- Quality Factor (Q): Systems utilize high-Q resonators (defined as Q greater than 100)
- Geometric Mean Requirement: sqrt(Q1*Q2) greater than 100 for efficient coupled systems
- Strong-Coupling Factor (U): U greater than 0.2 gives greater than 1% efficiency; U greater than 9 gives greater than 80% efficiency; U greater than 45 gives greater than 95% efficiency Frequency Range:
- Operating frequencies specified as below 10 GHz
- Examples demonstrate MHz-range operation Resonator Components:

attributes.text:
Inductive Element: For a circular single-turn loop: L approximately mu0*x*(ln(8x/a) - 2), where x is radius of enclosed surface and a is conductor radius. Capacitive Elements: Discrete capacitor plates or distributed capacitance between multi-loop windings. Fixed or variable implementations for tuning. DISTANCE AND COUPLING - Designed for mid-range distances from centimeters to meters
- Coupling-time between resonators much shorter than resonators' loss-times
- Distance D between source and device resonators measured in multiple system examples
attributes.parent_title: Wireless Energy Transfer for Supplying Power and Heat (WiTricity, 2014)

attributes.text: Unlike broadcast radiation which propagates to infinity (subject to losses), this near-field coupling scheme requires the receiver to be within the near-field region of the transmitter. The coupling is between two specific resonators, not a general broadcast. RESONATOR TYPES

attributes.text:
Magnetic Resonators (Primary Focus):
Electric field energy confined within structure; magnetic field energy extends into surrounding region. The patent notes these are preferred for wireless energy transfer applications in populated environments because most everyday materials including animals, plants, and humans are non-magnetic (i.e., relative permeability mu_r approximately 1), so their interaction with magnetic fields is minimal. Electric Resonators (Alternative):
Magnetic field energy confined; electric field extends outward. Can be used when magnetic resonators are impractical. SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE

attributes.text: Basic Configuration: A source resonator connected to power generator transfers energy wirelessly to a device resonator connected to a load, with both resonators designed to exchange energy wirelessly through their coupled magnetic near-fields.

Scaling Capability:

- Intermediate repeater resonators extending range
- Device resonators may receive energy from a source resonator, convert a portion of that energy to electric power for powering or charging a device, and simultaneously pass a portion of the received energy onto other device or mobile device resonators. IMPEDANCE MATCHING

- Resonator Q-factors are high

To all whom it may concern:
Be it known that I, GUGLIELMO MARCONI, of 71 Hereford Road, Bayswater, in the county of London, England, electrician, have invented Improvements in Transmitting Electrical Impulses and Signals and in Apparatus Therefor, (for which I have obtained Provisional Protection in Great Britain, by Letters Patent No. 12,039, dated June 2, 1896,) of which the following is a specification.
attributes.parent_title: Transmitting Electrical Signals (Marconi, 1896/1897)

attributes.text: According to this invention electrical actions or manifestations are transmitted through the air, earth, or water by means of electric oscillations of high frequency. The apparatus employed at the transmitting-station consists of an induction-coil or equivalent means for producing electric oscillations and a radiator for directing the oscillations through the air. The radiator comprises a metallic surface or plate elevated above the ground and connected to one terminal of the spark-gap of the induction-coil. The other terminal of the spark-gap is connected to the earth.
attributes.parent_title: Transmitting Electrical Signals (Marconi, 1896/1897)

attributes.text: When the induction-coil is excited sparks pass across the spark-gap and electric oscillations are set up in the circuit comprising the elevated plate and the earth connection. These oscillations cause the emission of electromagnetic waves which are propagated outward through space. At the receiving-station a similar arrangement of elevated plate and earth connection is employed, connected to a coherer or other detector responsive to the incoming electromagnetic waves. The electromagnetic waves striking the receiving plate induce oscillatory currents therein which actuate the detector.
attributes.parent_title: Transmitting Electrical Signals (Marconi, 1896/1897)

attributes.text: Figure 1 of the accompanying drawings shows the transmitting apparatus. A is an induction-coil of any suitable type. B is the spark-gap across which sparks pass when the coil is excited. One terminal of the spark-gap is connected to a metallic plate C elevated above the ground on a pole or mast. The other terminal is connected to a metal plate D buried in the earth or otherwise connected to earth.
attributes.parent_title: Transmitting Electrical Signals (Marconi, 1896/1897)

attributes.text: Figure 2 shows the receiving apparatus. E is a coherer of the Branly type comprising a glass tube containing metal filings. F is the receiving plate elevated on a pole. G is the earth connection. H is a battery and relay for operating a signaling device J such as a Morse inker.

attributes.text: The action of the apparatus is as follows. When sparks pass in the transmitting spark-gap electromagnetic waves are emitted in all directions. Those waves which strike the receiving plate induce currents which cause the metal filings in the coherer to cohere and become conducting. The current from the battery then flows through the coherer and the relay, and the relay operates the signaling device.
