attributes.text: The range of transmission depends upon the height of the transmitting and receiving plates, the power of the induction-coil, and the sensitivity of the coherer. With the apparatus described signals have been transmitted over distances of several miles. For improved transmission over longer distances the elevated plates may be replaced by vertical wires or antennae, and the induction-coil may be replaced by a transformer of higher power. The electromagnetic waves radiated from such an apparatus propagate in all directions with decreasing intensity as the distance from the transmitter increases.

attributes.text: The electromagnetic waves produced by the apparatus are of the Hertzian type, being electromagnetic radiation capable of propagating through free space. attributes.text: In my application Serial No. 252,133, filed October 12, 1887, I have shown and described a mode or plan of operating electrical motors by means of alternating currents which involved a novel method of transforming and transmitting electrical energy. In my present application I have described a method and apparatus for the electrical transmission of power constituting a modification of said plan and possessing certain new characteristics.
attributes.parent_title: Electrical Transmission of Power - AC Polyphase (Tesla, 1887/1888)

attributes.text: The transmission of power by means of alternating currents of electricity, which has been heretofore proposed, has usually been performed by employing a single alternating-current circuit extending from the generator to the motor or translating device. This single circuit, when the distance between generator and motor is considerable, presents many disadvantages, chief among which are the loss of power by leakage and the difficulty of maintaining the proper synchronism between the generator and motor.
attributes.parent_title: Electrical Transmission of Power - AC Polyphase (Tesla, 1887/1888)

attributes.text: I have found that these disadvantages may be obviated and the efficiency of the transmission greatly increased by employing, in place of the single circuit, a system of multiple circuits conveying currents differing in phase, and connecting the generator and motor by means of such a system. In this way I obtain a transmission of power which is practically independent of the distance and which is free from the losses which attend the ordinary method.
attributes.parent_title: Electrical Transmission of Power - AC Polyphase (Tesla, 1887/1888)

attributes.text: The motors which I employ in this system are of the type described in my application referred to. They consist of two or more sets of energizing-coils or helices placed upon a common field-magnet in such manner that the axes of the coils are at angles to each other, and adapted to be traversed by alternating currents differing in phase. The magnetic poles produced in the field-magnet are thereby caused to move or shift progressively around the field, setting up a rotating magnetic field in which an armature composed of a closed coil or a mass of iron is placed. The armature rotates in synchronism with the shifting poles, and thus constitutes the rotor of the motor.
attributes.parent_title: Electrical Transmission of Power - AC Polyphase (Tesla, 1887/1888)

attributes.text: In the present apparatus the generator is similarly constructed, having two or more sets of coils arranged at angles to each other and rotated in a magnetic field so as to generate alternating currents differing in phase. These currents are conveyed by separate circuits to the motor, where they energize the corresponding sets of coils therein and produce the rotating field which drives the armature.
attributes.parent_title: Electrical Transmission of Power - AC Polyphase (Tesla, 1887/1888)

attributes.text: Referring to the drawing, Figure 1 is a diagrammatic illustration of the transmitting and receiving apparatus. G is the generator, provided with two sets of coils a and b arranged at right angles to each other and rotated in the field of the magnet M. The two sets of coils produce alternating currents differing in phase by a quarter period. These currents are conveyed by the two independent circuits c and d to the corresponding sets of coils a' and b' in the motor M'. The motor has a rotating armature A which is driven by the rotating magnetic field produced by the coils a' and b'.
attributes.parent_title: Electrical Transmission of Power - AC Polyphase (Tesla, 1887/1888)

attributes.text: The important feature of this arrangement is that the circuits c and d are independent of each other, so that the current in one does not interfere with the current in the other. The result is that the motor runs in strict synchronism with the generator and the transmission is substantially loss-free. I have found this method of transmission particularly advantageous for the transmission of power over long distances, where the losses in the ordinary single-circuit system are prohibitive.
attributes.parent_title: Electrical Transmission of Power - AC Polyphase (Tesla, 1887/1888)

attributes.text: The details of the generator and motor construction are as follows. The generator has a field-magnet excited by a continuous current from a separate source. The armature comprises two sets of coils wound upon a common core and arranged at right angles to each other. As the armature rotates, each set of coils generates an alternating current, and since the coils are displaced by a quarter turn, the currents differ in phase by a quarter period.
attributes.parent_title: Electrical Transmission of Power - AC Polyphase (Tesla, 1887/1888)

attributes.text: The motor has a similar field-magnet, but in this case the field-magnet is stationary and the armature rotates within it. The field-magnet carries two sets of coils arranged at right angles to each other, and these are connected to the corresponding coils of the generator by the two independent circuits. The alternating currents in these coils produce a rotating magnetic field which drives the armature. What I claim is—
attributes.parent_title: Electrical Transmission of Power - AC Polyphase (Tesla, 1887/1888)

attributes.text: 1. The method of electrically transmitting power which consists in generating at a transmitting-station alternating currents differing in phase, conveying them by independent circuits to a receiving-station, and there energizing the coils of a motor arranged to produce a rotating magnetic field.
attributes.parent_title: Electrical Transmission of Power - AC Polyphase (Tesla, 1887/1888)

attributes.text: 2. The combination of a generator having two or more sets of coils arranged to produce alternating currents differing in phase, a motor having two or more sets of coils adapted to receive said currents and produce a rotating magnetic field, and independent circuits connecting the generator and motor.
attributes.parent_title: Electrical Transmission of Power - AC Polyphase (Tesla, 1887/1888)

attributes.text:
3. The method of transmitting power electrically between distant points which consists in generating at the transmitting-station by the rotation of a set of coils in a magnetic field, alternating currents differing in phase, and utilizing said currents at the receiving-station to produce by their joint action a progressive movement of the magnetic poles of a motor. UNITED STATES PATENT
MODERN DIPOLE ANTENNA FOR RADIO FREQUENCY TRANSMISSION
(Representative modern radio antenna patent — control sample) ABSTRACT
Disclosed is a dipole antenna for radio frequency transmission and reception in the range 100 MHz to 6 GHz, suitable for use in modern wireless communication systems including cellular, Wi-Fi, and satellite radio applications.
attributes.parent_title: Modern Dipole Antenna for RF Transmission (control, modern)

attributes.text:
BACKGROUND
Modern wireless communication relies on the transmission of radio frequency electromagnetic waves between antennas. A transmitting antenna converts electrical signals into electromagnetic radiation which propagates through free space to a receiving antenna, where it is converted back into electrical signals. The efficiency of this process depends on the impedance matching between the antenna and the feed line, the radiation pattern of the antenna, and the gain characteristics.
attributes.parent_title: Modern Dipole Antenna for RF Transmission (control, modern)

attributes.text: Conventional dipole antennas comprise two conductive elements excited at a common feed point. The length of each element is typically one-quarter of the operating wavelength, making the total antenna length half a wavelength at the operating frequency. This configuration is known as a half-wave dipole and exhibits an omnidirectional radiation pattern in the plane perpendicular to the antenna axis.
attributes.parent_title: Modern Dipole Antenna for RF Transmission (control, modern)

attributes.text:
SPECIFICATION
The present invention provides an improved dipole antenna comprising first and second conductive elements of length substantially equal to one-quarter of the free-space wavelength at the center operating frequency. The elements are arranged collinearly with a feed point at the center. A balun transformer is coupled to the feed point to convert the balanced antenna impedance to an unbalanced impedance compatible with coaxial feed lines.
attributes.parent_title: Modern Dipole Antenna for RF Transmission (control, modern)

attributes.text: The antenna is designed for operation at frequencies in the range 2.4 GHz to 5.8 GHz, covering common Wi-Fi and wireless LAN bands. At 2.4 GHz the wavelength in free space is approximately 125 mm, making each element approximately 31 mm in length. At 5.8 GHz the wavelength is 52 mm and each element is approximately 13 mm.
attributes.parent_title: Modern Dipole Antenna for RF Transmission (control, modern)

attributes.text: The radiation pattern exhibits the characteristic figure-eight shape in the H-plane with maximum radiation perpendicular to the antenna axis and null along the axis. The peak gain is approximately 2.15 dBi. The input impedance at resonance is approximately 73 ohms. Far-field electromagnetic waves are radiated from the antenna and propagate outward through space following the inverse-distance law for field strength (1/r) and the inverse-square law for power density (1/r²). The radiated energy is not bound to any waveguide and propagates independently of any receiver. CLAIMS

attributes.text: 1. A dipole antenna comprising first and second elongated conductive elements arranged along a common axis with a feed point disposed between them, each element having a length substantially equal to one-quarter of the operating wavelength in free space. 2. The antenna of claim 1, wherein the operating frequency is in the range 2.4 GHz to 5.8 GHz. 3. The antenna of claim 1, further comprising a balun transformer coupled to the feed point.

attributes.text: 4. The antenna of claim 1, wherein the radiation pattern comprises an omnidirectional lobe in the plane perpendicular to the common axis. 5. The antenna of claim 1, wherein the input impedance at the feed point is approximately 73 ohms at the center operating frequency. 6. A method of radiating electromagnetic waves comprising exciting a dipole antenna with an alternating current signal at the feed point of the antenna such that electromagnetic waves are emitted from the antenna elements and propagate outward into free space.

attributes.text: 7. The method of claim 6, wherein the alternating current signal has a frequency in the range 2.4 GHz to 5.8 GHz. 8. The method of claim 6, wherein the electromagnetic waves comprise far-field radiation characterized by a field strength that decays as 1/r with distance r from the antenna. 9. A wireless communication system comprising a transmitting dipole antenna and a receiving dipole antenna separated by a distance across which electromagnetic waves propagate as free-space radiation.
